severity.10: Hazardous. Fire, electrical or freezing damage to the building.
severity.8: High. Prolonged loss of temperature control in a heated zone.
severity.6: Moderate. Persistent comfort error, or a wrong value acted on silently.
severity.4: Low. One zone degraded while the rest of the cloud is unaffected.
severity.2: Minor. Information lost that nobody was acting on.

occurrence.10: Already the case. The defect is in the model as deployed.
occurrence.8: Frequent. Expected several times a year.
occurrence.5: Occasional. Expected once a year or so.
occurrence.3: Infrequent. Expected once in a few years.
occurrence.1: Remote. No reason to expect it.

detection.10: Undetectable. Nothing inside or outside the cloud would notice.
detection.8: Very poor. Visible only by reading the graph or the logs afterwards.
detection.5: Poor. A consumer sees a failure; nothing aggregates it into an alarm.
detection.3: Moderate. A heartbeat bounds the silence, but no alarm is raised.
detection.1: Certain. An alarm service reports it as it happens.

total-loss.means: The whole cloud stops: control, supervision, and the means of noticing, together.

loss-of-control.means: A heated zone can be driven to a value the building cannot survive, or driven not at all.

loss-of-input.means: A controller runs open-loop. It holds its last output while the room does as it pleases.

silent-wrong-control.means: The loop keeps running on a value that is no longer true. Worse than stopping, because nothing looks wrong.

wrong-by-design.means: A zone is regulated to another zone's condition. Both loops behave correctly and one room is uncomfortable.

silent-rule-failure.means: A rule that should pair two things does not, and its failure looks like a decision.

unused-information.means: Something is published and acted on by nobody. Its failure and its success look alike.

irreplaceable-capability.means: A capability that exists in one place only. When that place fails the capability is gone, and no amount of spare capacity elsewhere replaces it.

unplannable.means: The model does not say enough for anything to plan around it, so it must be assumed to be the worst case.

model-omission.means: Not a prediction. The omission is in the deployed model now.

model-inconsistency.means: Also already the case: two systems disagree in the graph as it stands.

configuration-typo.means: Present in the configuration as written.

architectural-choice.means: A deliberate decision whose consequence is permanent until it is revisited.

device-unavailable.means: A wireless sensor, its battery, its link or its bridge. Expected about once a year.

upstream-stalled.means: A polling loop stops or a source goes quiet without saying so.

host-failure.means: Grid outage or hardware failure. Rural supply, and correlated with the winter storms when heat matters most.

unobservable-from-within.means: Nothing inside the cloud can report it, because the reporting stopped too.

no-constraint.means: The write succeeds. The result looks like ordinary operation.

no-staleness-signal.means: A value that stopped changing and a value that stopped arriving are the same value.

published-not-consumed.means: Nothing consumes it, so nothing can observe that it failed.

no-validation.means: Nothing checks the literal at registration or at graph assembly.

graph-only.means: Visible by reading the graph. Nothing detects it at runtime.

heartbeat.means: A subscriber hears silence and can treat the publisher as gone, though no alarm is raised.
